title: Accepted
full_review:
If a movie could earn a college degree, the campus comedy "Accepted" (Universal) would graduate summa cum lousy.

Justin Long plays high school senior Bartleby "B" Gaines, a savvy slacker who, rejected by every school to which he applied, saves face by creating a fake college, forging an acceptance letter, a Web site and -- with the help of some friends (Jonah Hill, Columbus Short, Maria Thayer and Adam Herschman) -- transforming an abandoned hospital into a college campus.

His gullible parents (Mark Derwin and Ann Cusack) don't ask too many questions. They just write him a check for tuition and drop him off at his new "dorm." When they request a meeting with the school's dean, Bartleby recruits his buddy's iconoclast Uncle Ben (Lewis Black) to play the part.

The scheme snowballs out of control and a mob of self-described rejects and misfits shows up on the school's doorstep, testing even Bartleby's talent for thinking fast.

The semester plays out like one big poolside keg party. (Tuition is $10,000 a head, which Bartleby uses to buy booze and video games.)
